name: Відволікання (2)
description:
Ha! Your opponent might be a good defender, but you know what to do about that!

You already know that you can take the defender or chase it away. If that does not work, there is third tricky tactic. You can also lure away the defender.

The examples show how this is done.
In example 1, luring away is very similar to deflecting. But now, White first gives up one of his pieces. This makes it possible to take a stronger piece himself in the next turn.
In chess this is called a decoy sacrifice. Decoys can be very powerful!

Example 2 shows another type of luring away. This time, White does not have to sacrifice a piece. He takes advantage of an overloaded piece.
Overloading occurs when a single piece has two defensive jobs at the same time. It is simply too busy.

What do you have to do?
Beat the defender by luring it away.

examples.text:
White can take the queen but that does not win him any points. Black king will recapture. That's why White is going to beat this defender first.

How? By cheking the king with the Bishop. The king must abandon the queen.
Click on the play button to watch the moves.

Do you understand the difference between luring away and deflecting?
In luring away, White uses a decoy sacrifice (bishop) to make it possible to capture a stronger piece (queen).

Did you notice that White used a check for his decoy? Decoying the king is a smart trick. Your opponent is forced to react.

Here, White has a free capture. He does not even need to sacrifice material.

The black rook (yellow square) has two tasks.
It defends the rook and the knight. This defender is overloaded. It is too busy.
White takes advantage of the overload!
He takes the rook.
If the black rook recaptures, it abandons the knight. White can safely take it.
White wins material by luring away the defender.
